clue.text: Society leaders securing what could be a nicer situation

indicators.note: securing means holding something in, so the society letters wrap round the rest
the plural leaders asks for the opening pair of letters of the word Society, not just one
what could be signals that the letters of a nicer are to be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Smart society figures lock down a scenario that might turn out pleasanter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' in the plural takes two opening letters, not one; 'securing' wraps them round the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is an imagined sequence of events, a possible situation or setting.

clue.text: Tight-fisted players left in the UK

parts.note: near is an old word for stingy or mean with money
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: Mean players were dropped, in Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain traffic drives on the left, so the side of a car next to the kerb is the left side.
explanation.definitionFit: The nearside of a vehicle is the kerb side, which in Britain is its left-hand side.

clue.text: Tip off about a survey?

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the tip-off word goes round the a

parts.note: to tip off is to inform, to apprise someone

explanation.surface: Someone is warned about a coming survey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside APPRISE.
explanation.definitionFit: To survey a property or situation is to assess or evaluate it, which is what valuing means.

clue.text: Equipped for new work, danced energetically again?

definitions.meaning: a factory ... is refitted with new equipment for a different job

explanation.surface: Something refitted for a fresh task, or someone who has had another lively dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition splits the word as RE + JIGGED, a jig being a lively folk dance; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To rejig is to rearrange or re-equip something for a new purpose; the pun reads it as a repeated jig.

clue.text: Rodent (male) blocking source of his river repeatedly

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, so only the opening letter of his is used
blocking means sitting in the way, so the male letter goes between the two rivers
repeatedly tells us to write the river name twice over

parts.note: the Ouse is a river in Yorkshire, and another in southern England

explanation.surface: A male rodent dams the source of his river again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse, a crossword favourite, is written twice by 'repeatedly', and 'blocking' sets M between the two copies, after H.
explanation.definitionFit: The house mouse is the common small rodent found in human dwellings.

clue.text: Game Egyptian ruler once mentioned in speech

indicators.note: mentioned in speech signals that we want a word said like the ruler's title

parts.note: a pharaoh was a king of ancient Egypt

explanation.surface: A game is named after an ancient Egyptian king, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: Faro is an old gambling card game, said just like the Egyptian king's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Faro is a card game for gamblers, popular in nineteenth-century saloons.

clue.text: Rebellious worker rejected condition press chief put first

indicators.note: put first places the turned-round pair ahead of the worker
rejected means sent back, so the condition and editor are read backwards together

parts.note: if expresses a condition
the ED, or editor, is the head of a newspaper
an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: A defiant employee turns down a condition the editor insisted on first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns both the condition and the editor round together, giving DEFI, before the worker insect.
explanation.definitionFit: Being defiant means openly resisting authority, as a rebel does.

clue.text: Gang that is busy primarily installed connecting timber

indicators.note: installed means placed within, so these letters go inside the gang

parts.note: a gang is a team of workers
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so take the opening letter of busy

explanation.surface: A busy crew put in the joining beam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installed' puts the abbreviation and the first letter of busy inside the gang. A tie-beam is a roofing timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-beam is a horizontal timber joining the feet of rafters in a roof.

clue.text: Marker young chap placed outside university

indicators.note: placed outside means the young chap is wrapped round the university letter

parts.note: a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A lad stationed outside college leaves a sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'placed outside' puts BOY around U.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoy is a floating marker anchored to show a channel or hazard at sea.

clue.text: Executive from Mali involved with Reagan?

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so the letters of the two names are mixed together

explanation.surface: Some top manager in Mali has dealings with President Reagan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved with' mixes up the letters of MALI and REAGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Executive as an adjective means having to do with management or administration.

clue.text: Evade dispute, creating border

parts.note: to hedge is to dodge giving a straight answer
a row is a quarrel or argument

explanation.surface: Dodging an argument produces a dividing line.
explanation.definitionFit: A hedgerow is a line of bushes forming the boundary of a field or road.

clue.text: Liquid food originally cooked on battlefield?

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so take the opening letter of cooked

parts.note: taken as written
the Somme in northern France was a great First World War battlefield

explanation.surface: Soup first cooked out in the trenches?
explanation.walkthrough: The Somme is the French river where a huge 1916 battle was fought; the question mark flags it as one example of a battlefield.
explanation.definitionFit: Consommé is a clear soup, a liquid food made from concentrated stock.

clue.text: Standards in English broadcast brought back after review

indicators.note: after places the reversed part behind the review

parts.note: a crit is a short informal word for a critique or review

indicators.note: brought back means returned, so the broadcast and English letters run in reverse

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: Standards in a British broadcast are restored after an inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' reverses the broadcast-plus-English pair, giving ERIA; a crit is a casual word for a critique.
explanation.definitionFit: Criteria are the standards or tests by which things are judged.

clue.text: I must leave hosts dividing roast? Hard cheese!

indicators.note: dividing means splitting the roast word open with the rest

parts.note: to pan or roast something is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: must leave means the named letter has to go from the word

parts.note: a host is an army, so hosts are armies

explanation.surface: Told to leave the dinner party mid-roast, someone is told tough luck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard cheese!' is British slang for bad luck; here it literally defines a hard cheese. 'roast' is the verb meaning criticise.
explanation.definitionFit: Parmesan is a hard Italian cheese, the exclamation mark giving the slang phrase a literal reading.

clue.text: Caught escaping from crashed police car making horse jump

indicators.note: escaping from means the caught letter leaves the mix
crashed signals the car letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A caught suspect flees a wrecked police car, making a horse leap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaping from' takes C out of POLICE CAR, and 'crashed' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriole is a leap made by a trained horse, kicking out its hind legs at the top.

clue.text: Disheartened islanders thus smuggled climbing plants

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the whole run is read upwards
disheartened means losing the heart, so only the outer letters of islanders stay

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to mark a quotation as printed
to run goods is to smuggle them

explanation.surface: Gloomy islanders sneaked in creeping plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' leaves IS from islanders; 'climbing' reverses IS + SIC + RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcissi are flowering bulbs such as daffodils, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Endlessly bemoaning financial disaster

indicators.note: endlessly means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: rueing or ruing means regretting, bemoaning

explanation.surface: Endless complaining about a money crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' takes the last letter G off RUING.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruin is total loss of money and property, a financial collapse.

clue.text: Single Republican old American finds demanding

parts.note: one means single
US stands for American, of the United States

explanation.surface: One old Republican voter finds things tough going.
explanation.definitionFit: Onerous means burdensome, needing a lot of effort.

clue.text: In Paris I ultimately invite sweetheart round for tea

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the sweetheart goes round the other letters

parts.note: darling is a term of endearment for a sweetheart
je is French for I

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so take the last letter of invite

explanation.surface: A Frenchman asks his sweetheart round for a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Paris I' is the French pronoun; 'round' wraps the sweetheart around it and the last letter of invite.
explanation.definitionFit: Darjeeling is a fine black tea grown in the Himalayan foothills of India.

clue.text: Bring shame upon girl initially seeking gainful career

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name

indicators.note: initially picks the first letters of seeking and gainful

parts.note: to career is to rush or race along

explanation.surface: A girl brings dishonour by chasing a lucrative career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' here is the verb meaning to rush headlong, not a profession.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgrace someone is to bring dishonour upon them.

clue.text: Senior stable employee forks out grand for clearance

parts.note: the head is the senior person in charge

indicators.note: forks out means pays away, so the grand letter goes out of the employee

parts.note: a groom looks after horses in a stable
G is slang shorthand for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A senior stable hand pays out a thousand for clearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forks out' removes G from GROOM to leave ROOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Headroom is the vertical clearance above you, such as under a bridge.

clue.text: Roman term roughly describing sort of square where artists met

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the anagram goes round the square
roughly signals the letters of Roman term are rearranged

parts.note: a T-square is a draughtsman's ruler shaped like a T

explanation.surface: A rough Roman phrase describes a sort of square where painters gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' mixes ROMAN TERM, and 'describing' puts it round T.
explanation.definitionFit: Montmartre, the hill district of Paris, was home to artists such as Picasso and Toulouse-Lautrec.

clue.text: Waterbird depositing fish on head of country bumpkin

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the fish goes first

parts.note: a dab is a small flatfish

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of country

parts.note: a hick is an unsophisticated country person

explanation.surface: A water bird drops a fish on the head of a country yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: The dabchick is the little grebe, a small diving bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabchick is a little grebe, a small diving bird found on ponds and lakes.

clue.text: Given strong illumination, landed with provisions across lake

indicators.note: across means lying over, so the provisions are spread across the lake letter

parts.note: food means supplies or provisions
to light or alight is to land, so landed is lit

explanation.surface: A brightly lit ship landed with stores across the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' sets the provisions around the lake letter; landed means alighted, as a bird alights.
explanation.definitionFit: Floodlit means lit up by powerful floodlights, as a stadium is.

clue.text: He should deliver just what's needed in opening of song?

indicators.note: in places the needed thing inside the opening bar

parts.note: the first bar of music is bar one
it means exactly the thing wanted, as in that's it

explanation.surface: A singer gives exactly what's required at the start of the song?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opening of song' looks like a first-letter pick, but it means the first bar of the music; 'in' places the needed thing inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A baritone is a male singer, so he is someone expected to deliver a song.

clue.text: An accountant trained to rise in the scholastic world

parts.note: an gives the single letter a
CA is a chartered accountant

indicators.note: to rise in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: to train a gun is to aim it, so trained is aimed

explanation.surface: An accountant has been trained to climb in the academic world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' reverses AIMED into DEMIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Academia is the world of universities, scholars and research.

clue.text: Feature of mountain-top currently caught in deep ditch?

indicators.note: in places the present and caught letters inside the ditch

parts.note: a sap is a deep trench dug towards an enemy position
now means at present
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A mountain peak is now caught in a deep gully.
explanation.walkthrough: A sap is a military trench, a sense the solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A snowcap is the covering of snow on a mountain summit.

clue.text: Knot turning up in Aran knitwear

indicators.note: turning up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A knot surfaces in an Aran knitted sweater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses RANK, which runs across Aran and knitwear. An Aran is a chunky cable-knit sweater from the Aran Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: A knar is a knot or gnarl in wood, a crossword-only sense for many solvers.
